questions.q: In a Windows file search, the pattern *report*.xlsx will find:
options: All .xlsx files whose names contain the word report
All files of any type containing report
questions.solution: The asterisk matches any number of characters, so *report*.xlsx matches any Excel workbook with 'report' anywhere in its name - e.g. annual-report-2026.xlsx and report-final.xlsx.
questions.shortcut: Prefix * = anything before, suffix * = anything after; .xlsx at the end restricts the type.

questions.q: The superscript formatting shortcut in MS Word is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+Shift+= applies superscript (x squared style); Ctrl+= applies subscript (H2O style). Ctrl+Shift+S opens the Apply Styles box.
questions.shortcut: Shift pushes the number UP: Shift with = gives the raised (super) script.

questions.q: In Chrome and Edge, which shortcut opens the 'Clear browsing data' dialog?
questions.solution: Ctrl+Shift+Delete opens the dialog for clearing history, cookies and cached files. Shift+Delete is permanent file deletion in File Explorer, not a browser command.
questions.shortcut: Ctrl+Shift = the strong version; the strongest delete wipes browsing data.

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut to insert the current date into a cell (as a fixed value) is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+; stamps today's date; Ctrl+Shift+; stamps the time; Ctrl+D fills down from the cell above; Ctrl+T creates a table.
questions.shortcut: Semicolon = stamp. Shift makes it time instead of date.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The quality of the mangoes sold in these markets ___ improved this year.
questions.solution: The head noun is *quality* (singular); *of the mangoes sold in these markets* is only a descriptive phrase. A singular subject with present perfect needs **has improved**.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

They said, "Hurrah! We have won the trophy."
options: They said with joy that they have won the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they would win the trophy.
They exclaimed with joy that they had won the trophy.
They exclaimed with sorrow that they had won the trophy.
questions.solution: Hurrah → **exclaimed with joy**; present perfect → past perfect; we → they. B inverts the tone; C keeps the un-shifted 'have won'; D changes the tense to would.
questions.shortcut: Hurrah = joy, Alas = sorrow; then backshift the tense.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They have completed the project.
options: The project has completed by them.
The project has being completed by them.
The project have been completed by them.
The project has been completed by them.
questions.solution: Present perfect → **has/have been + V3**. The new subject 'the project' is singular → **has been completed**. B drops 'been'; C wrongly uses 'being' in a perfect slot; D agrees the verb with 'they' instead of the new subject.
questions.shortcut: Perfect row: has/have been + V3; agree with the NEW subject.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The union leader ___ every worker trusts was re-elected without a contest.
questions.solution: Rephrase the clause: 'every worker trusts (him)' — object role, person → **whom**. *Whose* shows possession, *which* serves things, *what* does not introduce such relative clauses.

questions.q: The main constituent of CNG (compressed natural gas) is:
questions.solution: CNG is mostly **methane**. LPG is mainly **butane** with propane.

questions.q: The **Subsidiary Alliance** system was introduced by —
questions.solution: **Lord Wellesley** (1798–1805) made Indian rulers keep British troops at their own cost and accept a British Resident; the Nizam of Hyderabad signed first (1798).

questions.q: The Telugu work ***Amuktamalyada*** was written by which Vijayanagara ruler?
questions.solution: **Krishnadevaraya** (Tuluva dynasty) wrote *Amuktamalyada*, about the Alvar saint Andal. His court had the eight poets called **Ashtadiggajas**.

questions.q: The writ of 'quo warranto' is issued to:
options: release a person from illegal detention
direct a public official to perform his duty
question the legality of a person holding a public office
quash the order of a lower court
questions.solution: **Quo warranto** literally means 'by what authority' — it prevents a person from unlawfully occupying a public office. Release from illegal detention is *habeas corpus*; commanding performance of duty is *mandamus*; quashing a lower court's order is *certiorari*.
questions.shortcut: warranto ~ 'where is your warrant to hold this post?'

questions.q: The length of a rectangle increases by 20% and the breadth decreases by 10%. The percentage change in its area is:
questions.solution: $\Delta\%=20-10-\frac{20\times10}{100}=+8\%$ — an 8% increase.
questions.shortcut: $20-10-2=+8$. Traps: 10% (ignores the cross term), 'no change' (assumes cancellation).

questions.q: How much water costing nothing must be added to 60 litres of milk at ₹24 per litre so that the mixture is worth ₹20 per litre?
questions.shortcut: Water is the 0-price ingredient: alligate ⇒ 5 : 1 ⇒ 12 L.

questions.q: Two mobile phones are sold at ₹1,200 each — one at a profit of 25% and the other at a loss of 25%. The overall result is:
What is the highest power of 12 that divides $50!$?
questions.solution:
$12 = 2^2 \times 3$.
Power of 2 in 50!: $25 + 12 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 47$ → number of $2^2$ blocks $= \lfloor 47/2 \rfloor = 23$.
Power of 3 in 50!: $16 + 5 + 1 = 22$.
Highest power of 12 $= \min(23, 22) = 22$.

questions.q: A cube of side 5 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many small cubes have **exactly one** face painted?
questions.solution: Each face has a (5 − 2) × (5 − 2) = 9 block of cubes with only that face painted. 6 faces × 9 = **54**.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 154 118" width="154" height="118" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="5" y2="113"/><line x1="5" y1="113" x2="149" y2="113"/><line x1="149" y1="113" x2="77" y2="5"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="53" y2="113"/><line x1="77" y1="5" x2="101" y2="113"/><line x1="41" y1="59" x2="113" y2="59"/></svg>
questions.solution: Two apex lines give (3 × 4)/2 = 6 triangles above the base. The horizontal line crosses all apex lines and creates another complete set of 6 above it. Total 6 × 2 = **12**.

questions.q: **'birds fly high' = 'lo pe ni'**, **'high skies shine' = 'ni ta co'**, **'birds shine bright' = 'pe co ra'**. What is the code for **birds**?
questions.solution: Sentence 1: birds fly high → lo pe ni. Sentence 3: birds shine bright → pe co ra. 'birds' is common to 1 and 3, whose common code-word is **pe** ('high' = ni sits in sentences 1-2; 'shine' = co in 2-3) → birds = **pe**.
questions.shortcut: Overlap coding: the code-word shared by exactly the sentences sharing the word.

questions.q: **A is 5 km North of B. C is 5 km East of A.** In which direction is **C from B**?
questions.solution: B at origin → A at (0, 5) → C at (5, 5). Both components positive → **North-East** of B (7.07 km away, if asked).
questions.shortcut: Chain from B, the asked-from point: up 5, right 5 → NE.
